value.hook: Open before writing any once-only send, notice, drain or watchdog step that must not double-send or be lost
value.title: Claim, send, stamp: one-shot notifications that survive races and restarts

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Shape used in #129 (role request claim) and #133 (s12 time-limit notices), and passed by review, security and performance:

1. Claim in one UPDATE whose WHERE also checks every guarding fact, for example: holder live with an open assignment (to_at IS NULL); answered_at IS NULL; stage not yet stamped; no live claim. Send only if a row changed. A read check earlier in the round is not a guard, because awaits sit between it and the send.
2. Send through ordinary delivery with a fixed msg_id per request and stage. Delivery answers a duplicate msg_id with Delivered (the ledger replays it), so a retry after a lost stamp is safe.
3. Stamp only once delivery admits the message (delivered, queued or held). On refusal or no recipient, release the claim (WHERE claim = mine) so the next round retries.
4. A daemon that stops mid-attempt leaves a claim: give it a lease (LIMIT_CLAIM_LEASE_MS), or recover intermediate states at boot (recover_delivering_role_requests). Index every evidence probe and assert it with an in-crate EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN test (SEARCH using <index>, no SCAN); performance checks this.
5. To test a stale-snapshot race without hooks, expose the per-item step (time_limit_step) and drive it with a snapshot read before the competing write.
Code: crates/store/src/role_requests.rs, crates/daemon/src/delivery/role_send.rs. Tests: directory_http limit_rig and the a_*_retried / stopped-daemon cases.
